notes.title: BREAKDOWN EDITION
notes.notes:
In version 6.0 of PSYCHOLOG (the Breakdown Edition), several small cutscenes and sounds have been added, bringing the inner life of the protagonist to the fore.

A reported minor bug has been fixed, as well as minor issues with American vs English spelling.

notes.title: PHOBIA EDITION
notes.notes:
In [b]version 5.0[/b] of [b]PSYCHOLOG[/b] (the Phobia Edition), the suffocating atmosphere of the city is heightened through several new scene additions scattered across the story.

The user interface has received a visual overhaul.

A few weird bugs have been fixed, including Ashley’s resurrection during the second week.

Additional minor issues have also been addressed.

notes.title: ANXIETY EDITION
notes.notes:
What happens when, as a psychologist, you realize that your clients may have turned against you? Or that your colleagues can no longer be trusted?

In [b]version 4.0[/b] of [b]PSYCHOLOG[/b] (the "Anxiety Edition"), the story deepens with several new scenes that further make you question the meaning of everyday routines.

Additionally, several minor issues have been fixed.

notes.title: TRAUMA EDITION
notes.notes:
What happens when, as a psychologist, you start losing your objectivity? When the problems of your clients begin to affect you more than you can help them?

In [b]version 3.0[/b] of [b]PSYCHOLOG[/b] (the "Trauma Edition"), the story deepens with several new scenes that subtly hint at the forces behind the mysterious events haunting the small therapy practice.

The city itself takes on a greater role, becoming almost a character in its own right.

notes.title: Version 2.0 released
notes.notes:
With [b]version 2.0[/b] (the "Paranoia Edition"), the game is updated in several ways. 

[h2]A Fleshed-Out Narrative[/h2]
The [b]addition of several shorter scenes[/b] throughout the narrative aims to subtly shift the focus of the story, highlighting the protagonist's role in the unfolding drama. [b]More hotspots[/b] have been added to point-and-click scenes, increasing the overall level of interactivity.

[h2]Introduction of Difficulty Modes[/h2]
Players can now choose between three different difficulty settings at the start of the game, affecting how clients react to dialogue during therapy sessions. In [b]Trainee[/b] mode, your choice of words is less critical, giving you more leeway to explore different approaches. In the [b]Licensed Professional[/b] mode (corresponding to "normal" difficulty), decisions will have a more noticeable impact on the outcome, requiring closer attention to each client's needs and responses. Finally, in [b]Seasoned Practitioner[/b] mode, clients are harder to impress, building trust takes time, and the treatment requires precision, as the margin for error is minimal.

[h2]Dynamic Visuals[/h2]
To sum up the graphical changes made in several updates since launch: the [b]introduction of subtle motion[/b] in displayed scenes makes the oppressive, urban setting less static. Additionally, during point-and-click scenes, players can slightly move around inside the scene by moving the cursor. Several minor tweaks to the game engine aim to make scene transitions smoother.

notes.title: Demo now available
notes.notes: Experience the gameplay and the oppressive atmosphere of PSYCHOLOG in this stand-alone demo. In the full game, you take on the role of a psychologist tasked with improving the lives of five vulnerable individuals. Among them is Vera Mills, a woman who lives alone in a small apartment, avoiding neighbors, seldom looking at herself in the mirror, and often mixing things up. This short demo offers a glimpse into the events leading up to her decision to finally seek help.
